correctness.rationale: For any graph with girth >=6 and n>=6, the Alexander dual has complete 2-skeleton, no faces of size 5, and a distinct free triangle in every connected-four-set tetrahedron. Collapsing all tetrahedra gives a simply connected two-complex with free second-homology rank binomial(n-1,3) minus the claw and induced-P4 count; integral Alexander duality gives original four-cut homology, and a full lower skeleton plus Hurewicz and Whitehead gives the wedge for n>=8 (and graph case n=6). The full proof treats n=7 only in homology. The standalone verifier checks the lemma and direct finite mod-2 chains, including all 2992 six-vertex graphs satisfying girth, and returns VERIFY_OK.

originality.rationale: The published general Euler/skeleton/two-possible-degrees theorem does not determine whether codimension-one homology vanishes; this result proves its vanishing for all girth-at-least-six graphs using one free triangle per induced connected four-set and, for n >= 8, upgrades to a wedge homotopy theorem. Existing forest, cycle, Heawood-specific and rectangular-grid calculations are not claimed as new. Exact published-source and related-result comparisons were conducted, subject to residual risk of unindexed equivalents.

value.rationale: A natural, unbounded graph class obtains complete topological classification of ordinary four-cut complexes, not just Euler data; arbitrary girth-at-least-six cubic graphs of the same vertex count have identical homotopy types. The degree-and-edge multiplicity links topology to induced four-vertex trees and subsumes isolated known forest, cycle, and Heawood cases. This unifies genuinely different graph structures and can guide further study of graph cut topology without requiring a downstream paper-sized application.
